newsitem.title: FRANCE: Annan to urge U.N. force for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Annan to urge U.N. force for Zaire.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, encouraged by France, said on Friday he hoped to persuade member states to reconsider sending a multinational force to eastern Zaire in the light of a very serious humanitarian situation.
But U.N. officials questioned whether the United States and other powers would be more willing to send troops into the war-torn jungle region than they had been last December.

"I hope with this information we can persuade member states to reconsider the decision to cancel the multinational force for eastern Zaire," Annan told reporters after talks with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.

Annan said he had no precise information about reported massacres of Rwandan Hutu refugees in the Kivu province where Ugandan-backed Tutsi rebels are fighting Zaire government forces but he said "the humanitarian situation is very serious".

The new U.N. chief, on his inaugural visit to Paris, said the international community had not shown a sufficient political will to send the force created by a U.N. resolution in November but he would take the issue up again on his return to New York.

Plans to send the force, for which a Canadian general had been appointed commander, collapsed when many of an estimated 1.2 million refugees from neighbouring Rwanda and Burundi returned home of their own accord last year.
But hundreds of thousands remain trapped in Zaire with little food or water and reports published in the French and Belgian press this week suggested there had been massacres.

De Charette, who called the world "spineless" last November for its reluctance to send a force, said France was gravely concern about the humanitarian situation in eastern Zaire, saying an immediate halt to fighting was essential.
He called for an international investigation into reported "tragedies" in the region, adding "this is a matter of great urgency".
The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Thursday it had no independent confirmation of reported killings in eastern Zaire, where the war has restricted U.N. staff movements.

Belgian Development and Cooperation Minister Reginald Moreels told Het Laatste Nieuws newspaper at the weekend he had received eyewitness reports that a new "genocide" was under way in East Zaire and that mass graves had been found.

UNHCR spokesman Fernando del Mundo said a Zairean agency, Equilibre, reported it had found 6,800 bodies of Rwandan Hutus and Zaireans during a six to eight week period after the fall of the border town of Goma late last year to Tutsi-led rebels.
On Thursday, Annan had said that the international community lacked will at this time to send troops. "One cannot send in a force without the will," he told France 2 television.

Diplomats said his more positive tone on Friday may have reflected a desire to please France, the last U.N. Security Council power to accept his candidacy after fighting in vain for the re-appointment of his predecessor, Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt.

Annan's special envoy, Mohammed Sahnoun, has been in South Africa this week working with President Nelson Mandela on a diplomatic drive for peace talks in the Great Lakes region. He flew to Paris on Friday to report to the U.N. chief.

Annan said there were no plans for either himself or Sahnoun to talk to ailing Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is at his French Riviera villa for further medical treatment after prostate cancer surgery last August.

Zaire has accused Uganda and Tutsi-led Rwanda and Burundi of militarily supporting the rebels, many of whom are ethnic Tutsis. Zaire's three eastern neighbours have denied involvement in the war, which began last October.
